reason: Layer order beats specificity: base comes before components, so the ID rule in base still loses. The misplaced assumption is that the ID selector wins — move the rule to a later layer or fix the layer order instead.
@import must appear before all other rules in a stylesheet, including at-rules like @layer. After the @layer block it is ignored entirely.
Every nesting level adds descendant specificity: this flattens to .task-manager .task-list .task-list__item — the spiral again. A flat single-class selector keeps the architecture maintainable.
The unlayered !important rule beats the layered rule, so the component style never applies. Remove the !important and let the layer order decide.

The layer order declaration is missing at the top of the file. Without an explicit order, layers win in the order they are first encountered — fragile and file-order dependent. Declare @layer base, components; first.
